english.title: In course food business keep at food premises cooked / reheated food at a temp below 63°C
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), in the course of the activities of a food business, kept at or in food premises at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION OF FOOD PREMISES..), at a temperature below 63°C, food, namely **(..SPECIFY FOOD..), which had been cooked or reheated, was for service or on display for sale and needed to be kept at or above 63°C in order to control the growth of pathogenic micro-organisms or the formation of toxins
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 17(2) of and paragraph 6 of Schedule 4 to the Food Hygiene (Wales) Regulations 2006.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Two Years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
No prosecution for an offence under these Regulations which is punishable under paragraph (2) of regulation 17 may be begun after the expiry of (a) three years from the commission of the offence; or (b) one year from its discovery by the prosecutor, whichever is the earlier.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
